sections.description: Full-coverage Rank Math SEO abilities for MCP. Per-post SEO metadata (core, robots, social, schema), settings, redirections, 404 monitor, sitemap tools, module toggling and analytics status.
sections.changelog:
2.2.0

  • Behaviour change: update-post-schema no longer stores a WooCommerceProduct block on a WooCommerce product. Rank Math discards that schema on the front end and rebuilds the Product entity from the product itself, so the write reported success while changing nothing observable. The verb now returns schema_ignored_by_target and names the fields that do drive the output. Pass force_ignored_type: true to store it anyway, for example to populate the Schema editor in wp-admin.
  • On a WooCommerce product, update-post-seo's seo_title also sets the Product schema name; when it is empty the name falls back to the pt_product_title template. The description now says so.
  • list-redirections search now matches a source pattern as well as the target URL, the way Rank Math's own list does.
  • Rank Math 1.0.278 added three read-only native abilities. rank-math/get-redirections overlaps this bridge only partly: its all status resolves to not trashed, so no native call reaches a trashed redirection, and the write verbs have no native counterpart. The affected descriptions now record where the boundary is.
  • Tested against WordPress 7.1, MCP Adapter 0.6.1 and Rank Math 1.0.278.

2.1.0

  • Nine ordinary settings were being hidden as if they were secrets: the sensitive-key pattern matched the "auth" inside "author", so author_robots, url_author_base, disable_author_archives and their siblings could be neither read nor written. Checked against all 182 keys in the four settings groups; only indexnow_api_key is redacted now.
  • update-settings now refreshes Rank Math's own settings object after writing. It previously left everything reading Helper::get_settings() in the same request looking at the old value, with no error to show for it.
  • Descriptions of the four abilities that overlap Rank Math 1.0.277's new native settings abilities now name the counterpart and the difference. Nothing was removed.
  • Declared a type for the untyped value properties, which stops core's schema validator warning on every call.

2.0.4

  • Fixes silently stale sitemaps after programmatic writes. Rank Math only registers its sitemap cache watcher when is_admin() or wp_doing_cron() is true, so nothing invalidates the cached sitemap XML for writes made over the REST API (which is how this bridge — and the block editor itself — saves) or WP-CLI. This bridge now registers the same hooks in those contexts and routes them to Rank Math's own public Cache_Watcher methods rather than implementing its own cache clearing.
  • Covers posts, terms and authors, not just posts. Multiple writes in one request coalesce into a single cache invalidation via Rank Math's own queue and shutdown drain.
  • Verified end to end over HTTP: with a warm cache, creating 3 posts left post-sitemap.xml serving 4 URLs; after this fix the same URL returns 7.

2.0.3

  • Fixed the MCP Adapter's execute-ability tool masking schema errors as a generic "Permission denied": get-post-seo, update-post-seo, update-post-social, update-post-schema and delete-post-schema now accept id (preferred) alongside post_id (deprecated alias, kept for backward compatibility), and return a clear WP_Error when neither is provided instead of silently defaulting to 0.

2.0.2

  • Security audit: strip_sensitive() no longer removes a matched key outright. A key like connect_data matches on its own name (contains connect) even though most of what it holds isn't secret; silently dropping the whole key made sibling data disappear with no indication it ever existed. The matched key's value is now replaced with a REDACTED marker instead — not a leak fix (nothing new is exposed), an output-honesty fix.

2.0.1

  • CRITICAL: fixed a data-corruption bug — update-post-seo, update-post-social, update-post-schema and bulk-update-seo-meta were not wp_slash()-ing content before writing to update_post_meta(), causing WordPress's own unslash step to strip literal backslashes from SEO metadata. Fixed at every affected call site. Settings and redirections/404 monitor were verified safe and left untouched.

2.0.0

  • Initial public release: 24 abilities covering post SEO metadata, settings, redirections, 404 monitor, sitemap and module toggling.
